Not published.** Marg Gardiner · Council · incumbent (held City office 2022–26). Scored 2 Sep 2026 against **The Program — A City That Works v1.10 (31 Jul 2026)** using the 12-topic template and Decision 14. **The letter on this card is a dash.** An internal proposal sits at the bottom of the page and is Joa's to apply or reject. Alignment compute APPLIED letter for Gardiner stays **D**. Incumbent: Record in the cell; a sourced miss caps below Close (max Partial+ 1.5). Do not stamp campaign 9.24 / 13.43 or the \$300M→\$160M reserve claim as ACTW figures. Lock is 13.3 → **7.28 overall / 9.34 residential / 4.78 business**. ## Card

### The five doors (front of the live card) Each door is **said / record / yes / —**: a sourced sentence or a fact. Never a second grade.
Door Measure said / record / yes / — sentence or fact URL date
Tax cap M66 **said** "Zero base all budget items with a view to holding tax increases to cost of living increases." Named NO on the 7 May 2026 budget (7.28 overall / 9.34 residential). Her reason is process and spending, not Kim's "tax hike was simply not enough." [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-passes-budget-in-debate-that-hints-at-start-of-election-campaign-12259094](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-passes-budget-in-debate-that-hints-at-start-of-election-campaign-12259094) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 7 May 2026 / press 9 May 2026
Downtown order M26 / M27 **said** "I have been a strong supporter of more bylaw and police enforcement on our streets." No Public Order Team and no 6am–10pm bylaw hours. The bylaw sentence is scored on M33, not here. [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
Housing M6 **said** "Review and amend housing bylaws to conform with the minimum housing dictates of the Province (e.g. the City's Missing Middle provides for 50% more units than the Provincial mandate)." Record: named NO, 26 Jan 2023. [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-adopts-divisive-missing-middle-housing-program-6443676](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-adopts-divisive-missing-middle-housing-program-6443676) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 26 Jan 2023 / press 27 Jan 2023
Household bill M66d **—** Water, sewer, stormwater and the combined household number do not appear. — —
Written program — **yes** Authorized 2026 campaign site with four named priorities, a plan-bullet list, a voting-record page and a current donate/volunteer ask. Written and current. No costed budget, no unit target, no implementation calendar. The \$300M→\$160M reserve sentence is a campaign claim, not a verified City figure. [https://marggardiner.ca/](https://marggardiner.ca/) · [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) retrieved 2026-09-02
--- ## The 12 topics No topic gets its own letter. Area columns stay blank. Rules as written on . Column key: **answer** = the mark · **quote or fact** = the verbatim sentence, then context · **URL** · **date**. A dash is unknown, not a fail. ### 1 · Housing that gets built
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
1 M6 housing supply + composition **Opposed −1.0** "Review and amend housing bylaws to conform with the minimum housing dictates of the Province (e.g. the City's Missing Middle provides for 50% more units than the Provincial mandate)." · Disagrees with M6 supply: the 2026 ask is to cut City housing bylaws down to the provincial floor. Record matches, not a miss: named NO with Coleman and Hammond, 26 Jan 2023. Context, same article, not a second mark: she tried to refer the motion and called it "a flawed concept." Context, same Plan page, not scored separately: "set housing targets more in line with current projected population increases." [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-adopts-divisive-missing-middle-housing-program-6443676](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-adopts-divisive-missing-middle-housing-program-6443676) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 26 Jan 2023 / press 27 Jan 2023
2 M6b land bank + co-ops — City land, a land bank and co-op financing do not appear in the 2026 Plan. Tenant displacement from assembly is diagnosis inside the housing-density paragraph, used as context on row 1, not a land-bank instrument. — —
3 M7 permits + AI pre-screening — No permit-time position, no published standard, nothing on AI pre-screening. Opposition to staff-issued permits sits inside the Delegation Bylaw sentence on row 53. — —
4 M7b pattern-book housing — Pre-approved designs and an expedited stream do not appear. — —
5 M8/M8b 5% vacancy, DCC cuts, suite amnesty — No vacancy target, no DCC position, no suite amnesty. — —
### 2 · Downtown order
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
6 M26 Public Order Team — No unified command, co-location, or downtown operations desk. "More bylaw and police enforcement" is scored once, on row 10 (M33). — —
7 M26b civilian crisis response — "Hiring of police officers who can handle traditional police work as well as outreach to street communities" puts outreach on sworn officers. That is not a civilian crisis-response capacity. Scored on row 33 as police funding, not here. — —
8 M27 bylaw hours 6am–10pm — More bylaw presence is named. Hours and a 6am–10pm standard are not. Enforcement without hours is scored on M33. — —
9 M28 data-targeted enforcement — No position on targeting chronic disorder drivers with data. — —
10 M33 daytime sheltering bylaws **Close 2.0** "We have the bylaws to ensure safe streets. We need to enforce them." · Commits to enforcing existing bylaws. Comparable, not Same: daytime sheltering is not named. 18 Jul 2024 motion passed 8–1 with Kim the lone named NO; Gardiner is not named in that article. Do not invent a YES. No sourced miss, so no incumbent cap. [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02
11 M33b drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure) **Partial 1.0** "Increase bylaw and police presence in neighbourhoods to enforce bylaws and laws regarding open use of illegal drugs." · Commits to open-use enforcement. Neither the buffer list nor child-focused geography is named. The Harbour closure motion is the SCS sentence already on row 23, not a second mark here. [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
12 M34–M37 encampments, reclaiming spaces, night lighting **Partial 1.0** "Ensure that the “solution” to street disorder downtown is not shifting encampments to neighbourhood park areas." · Commits to keeping encampments out of neighbourhood parks. No named-space protocol, no night-lighting programme, no removal sequence. [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 3 · Household bill
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
13 M66 tax glide path (capped on the residential rate) **Close 2.0** "Zero base all budget items with a view to holding tax increases to cost of living increases." · Commits to a COLA cap on tax increases. Comparable to M66's residential-rate glide path, not Same (no year-path, no override rule). ZBB in this sentence is already scored from the homepage on row 41 and is not a second mark. Record is a hit, not a miss: named NO on 7 May 2026 with Kim and Hammond. Do not copy Kim's "the tax hike was simply not enough" onto her. Her named reason: "Gardiner called the entire process flawed" and "We are digging ourselves into a hole while deceiving the public with soothing words about making Victoria a wonderful place to live." Adopted bill is 7.28 overall / 9.34 residential / 4.78 business. Do not stamp campaign 9.24 or 13.43 as ACTW figures. [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-passes-budget-in-debate-that-hints-at-start-of-election-campaign-12259094](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-passes-budget-in-debate-that-hints-at-start-of-election-campaign-12259094) · [https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/city-budget](https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/city-budget) · [https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 7 May 2026 / press 9 May 2026 and 11 May 2026
14 M66b/c over-collection refund + debt rule — No over-collection refund and no debt-rule / supermajority override. CHEK 3 Mar 2026 names her as voting against reducing the debt-reduction reserve to zero; that is a reserve-contribution vote, not M66c's debt rule, and is not scored here. — —
15 M66d the Household Bill — Water, sewer, stormwater and the combined household number do not appear. Aging-infrastructure is diagnosis in the tax paragraph, not a household-bill figure. — —
16 M70/M70b provincial downloading ledger — "The City must ensure that the Provincial government fulfils its responsibilities of health care and housing" is the same treatment-first package scored on row 23. One sentence-family, one measure. No downloading ledger and no published refusal table. — —
17 M70c CRD cost and the Goldstream plant — The CRD, regional water rates and the filtration plant do not appear. Committee seats (airport, SIPP) are a seat held, which the rules exclude. — —
18 M71–M73d business, downtown, one mandate not a new office — No vacancy target, no Strategic Economic Plan, no one-mandate-not-a-new-office. Meeting Fernwood and North Park business owners is campaign colour, not a City mandate. — —
19 M74/M75/M76 capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees — No 15-minute grace, no first-hour (Year 2 gated), no capital-approval threshold, no permit-fee schedule. — —
### 4 · Host Nations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
20 M1–M5 Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5. — No 2026 text on government-to-government tables, Indigenous procurement, place names, cultural protocols or an urban Indigenous liaison. City biography and committee list checked. A dash is still allowed. — —
### 5 · Homelessness and waitlists
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
21 M9/M9b/M64 tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated) — "As developers assemble land for larger developments, low-cost housing is demolished… often leading to tenant displacement" is a diagnosis of Missing Middle, already on row 1. No demoviction bylaw, no STR licensing, no indoor-heat standard. Mention, so a dash. M9c is struck. — —
22 M10 transparent algorithmic waitlists — Housing allocation and waitlists do not appear. Asking the Province to exempt supportive housing from the RTA is a tenancy-status ask, used as context on row 23, not a waitlist design. — —
23 M11 Housing First + STEP throughput **Opposed −1.0** "I am opposed to the spread of “safe” illicit drug consumption sites and low-barrier supportive housing that permits illicit drug use throughout Victoria." · M11 is Housing First (low-barrier supportive housing + STEP throughput). Explicit disagreement. Context, same Plan, not scored separately: phase out supportive housing that allows illicit drugs; convert to sober / drug-free treatment; accept only housing that leads to rehabilitation. Record matches: she moved to ask Island Health to cease The Harbour "at the earliest opportunity," lone YES, 2 Jul 2026. That is the SCS half of the same sentence, not a second mark. [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) · [https://cheknews.ca/victoria-motion-to-close-safe-consumption-site-defeated-7-1-1333838/](https://cheknews.ca/victoria-motion-to-close-safe-consumption-site-defeated-7-1-1333838/) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 2 Jul 2026 / press 2–3 Jul 2026
### 6 · Families
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
24 M12/M13b/M13c childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is \$0 → M13d) — Childcare spaces, family-doctor recruitment and the 18–25 cohort do not appear. M13 school food is \$0 and lives on M13d. — —
25 M13d standing School District 61 agreement — Campaign table claims she "Supported the re-introduction of the Police School Liaison Officer program." No independent press URL+date opened this pass. Do not invent a roll-call. SLO is not a standing SD61 agreement. Dash. — —
### 7 · Streets and mobility
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
26 M14/M16/M17/M18 cleanliness and the public realm — Graffiti, pests, sanitation hours and public art do not appear in the 2026 Plan. City biography's 2022 "cleaner and inviting" theme is 2022 Record, not a 2026 Plan cell. — —
27 M19/M22/M38/M40–M42b mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38) — No corridor, signal, intersection, school-zone or Vision Zero position. M39 is struck — not scored. Fire / single-egress is a building-code file, not this cluster, and is not in the 55. — —
28 M20b/M23b walking and transit the City controls — Walking, sidewalks, crossings and the City's own transit levers do not appear. — —
29 M24b/M25b accessibility and public washrooms — City biography lists accessibility among prior community-service files. That is professional / community background, which the rules exclude. No 2026 washroom or accessibility-audit sentence. — —
30 M25 fix roads first — "Aging infrastructure" appears only as a tax-pressure diagnosis. No backlog number, no pothole standard, no sequencing rule. Mention, so a dash. — —
### 8 · Policing and published safety
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
31 M28b business security cost-spreading — Business harm near The Harbour is context on row 23. No cost-spreading instrument. — —
32 M28d community paramedicine — Paramedicine and call-volume reduction do not appear. — —
33 M29/M29b VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force) **Partial 1.0** "Council must ensure that funding continues for foot patrols and the hiring of police officers who can handle traditional police work as well as outreach to street communities." · Commits to continued VicPD funding and hiring. No Esquimalt formula, no convene-and-publish regional review, no staffing number. Record is a hit, not a miss: named opposed to the 3 Mar 2026 4→2 cut, 5–4. "I support the police budget now and again this sleight of hand of ‘let's do two, as opposed to four,’ is a defund the police effort and I cannot support it at all." Context, same Plan, not scored separately: "I have opposed ‘defund the police’ motions." [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) · [https://cheknews.ca/victoria-approves-2-not-4-officers-for-vicpd-slashes-reserve-contributions-1309089/](https://cheknews.ca/victoria-approves-2-not-4-officers-for-vicpd-slashes-reserve-contributions-1309089/) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 3 Mar 2026 / press 3 Mar 2026
34 M30 smart LED lights, no surveillance — Streetlighting and the surveillance limit do not appear. — —
35 M31/M31b/M31c/M32 safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target — No safety dashboard, no published enforcement record, no crime-reduction number. "Measurable results" is inside the ZBB sentence on row 41. — —
### 9 · Beauty as a public good
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
36 M43–M46b heritage and cultural venues — Heritage-era housing "at risk" from Missing Middle is diagnosis inside the row 1 housing paragraph, not a heritage-standards or cultural-venue programme. — —
37 M45b/c pedestrianisation and the signature project — Pedestrianisation and a signature project do not appear. — —
38 M47–M49 heritage incentives, lighting, parks **Partial 1.0** "Review City amenities with an objective of providing green space and community amenities throughout the city — all based on population densities." · Commits to a green-space / amenities review tied to density. No heritage-incentive schedule, no ornamental lighting, no parks acreage number. Distinct sentence from the urban-forest bullet on row 49. [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
39 M50/M50b/M51/M52 culture, sport, and the arts funding floor — Arts, sport and a funding floor do not appear. Hanging-flower-basket photo is campaign colour, not a culture-funding cell. — —
### 10 · A smaller scored Hall
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
40 M15 managed competition — "Focus operations on Core Responsibilities of the City" names a lane, not competitive testing of City services. Lane is not a source. Absence of a managed-competition vote is Record, not Opposed. Clearest method-rhetoric gap on the card. — —
41 M65 rotating zero-based reviews **Close 2.0** "I will zero-base the budget and demand every dollar delivers measurable results for residents." · Commits to zero-based budgeting. Comparable, not Same: all-items ZBB, not rotating 3–4 areas, no three-part test. "Measurable results" in the same sentence is not a dashboard and is not scored on M67. Record matches: at the 7 May 2026 vote she "called for zero-based budgeting lens." No sourced miss (she voted NO on the non-ZBB bill), so no cap. [https://marggardiner.ca/](https://marggardiner.ca/) · [https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 7 May 2026 / press 11 May 2026
42 M67 quarterly performance dashboard — "Every dollar delivers measurable results" sits inside the sentence already scored on row 41. One sentence, one measure. No KPI set, no cadence, no dashboard. — —
43 M68 overhead reduction by attrition — Headcount, attrition and administrative overhead do not appear. Core-responsibilities is a Mention on row 40, not an attrition rule. — —
44 M69 real-estate rationalisation — City real-estate holdings do not appear. — —
45 M53/M53b/M53c GIS, AI consultation imagery, LIDAR — GIS, consultation imagery and LIDAR do not appear. MBA / data-analysis background is professional background, which the rules exclude. — —
46 M53d published municipal AI standard — Municipal use of AI does not appear. — —
47 M54–M57 local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging — Procurement, open data, Wi-Fi and EV charging do not appear. — —
### 11 · Climate and trees as operations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
48 M58/M58b/M64b climate, district energy, seismic — No 2026 climate-target, district-energy or seismic sentence. Climate Action Inter-Municipal Task Force is a seat held, which the rules exclude. — —
49 M59–M63 trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness **Close 2.0** "Review Urban Forest targets with the objective of increasing canopy cover beyond parks through enhanced tree plantings in neighbourhoods, on boulevards and on private property." · Commits to a canopy-increase review via plantings. Comparable to the trees half of M59–M63, not Same (no 5,000-tree number, no 35% canopy, no emergency-preparedness position). Record matches, not a second mark: she moved the 3 Apr 2025 canopy motion; Saanich News 4 Apr 2025: "In a pitch from Coun. Marg Gardiner, staff will add five-year tree canopy (growth) targets in the draft OCP supporting a 40 per cent, city-wide 2050 tree canopy goal." Campaign table restates that hit. OCP adoption NO (with Hammond and Coleman) is a density vote, not a trees miss. No sourced miss, so no cap. FLAG: Close is the high reading of "review with the objective of." [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) · [https://saanichnews.com/2025/04/04/a-developers-wet-dream-and-a-renters-nightmare-victoria-plans-for-growth/](https://saanichnews.com/2025/04/04/a-developers-wet-dream-and-a-renters-nightmare-victoria-plans-for-growth/) · [https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/filestream.ashx?DocumentId=101687](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/filestream.ashx?DocumentId=101687) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 3 Apr 2025 / press 4 Apr 2025
### 12 · Neighbourhoods and integrity
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
50 M77/M78/M78b \$25M referendum threshold, 5-step process, material-change rule — No \$25M threshold, no 5-step sequence, no material-change rule. Amalgamation is scored on row 55, not here. — —
51 M79/M79b Integrity Commissioner + 60-day consultation response — No Integrity Commissioner and no 60-day consultation-response standard. Delegation Bylaw / IAP2 / appeal rights are the neighbourhood-voice cluster on row 53, not this office. — —
52 M79c–f lobbyist registry, FOI fee, remuneration **Partial 1.0** "Eliminate planned generous salary increases for City Councillors and the Mayor, limiting increases to cost of living." · Commits to COLA-limited remuneration. No lobbyist registry, no FOI-fee position. Record matches: named opposed to the 1 Aug 2024 remuneration package with Hammond; on 13 Nov 2025 she moved to cap the mayor's salary to inflation, named YES in a 6–3 fail with Hammond and Coleman. Verbatim from that meeting: "We need to cut the budget and as council we need to lead by cutting the purse strings on ourselves." CPI-only is the motion, not a second quote. Cluster mark is Partial because two of three instruments are absent. [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-approves-recommended-pay-hike-9302383](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-approves-recommended-pay-hike-9302383) · [https://cheknews.ca/showdown-in-victoria-city-council-chambers-over-salaries-1289363/](https://cheknews.ca/showdown-in-victoria-city-council-chambers-over-salaries-1289363/) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 1 Aug 2024 / press 2 Aug 2024 · vote 13 Nov 2025 / press 13 Nov 2025
53 M80/M80b/M80c neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans **Close 2.0** "Re-introduce the IAP2 consultation process — involve people in decision-making rather than informing the public after decisions are made." · Commits to IAP2 as the neighbourhood-consultation instrument. Comparable, not Same: not official-languages access and not two Local Area Plans per year. Context, same Plan, not scored separately: "Give residents a greater say in the densification of their neighbourhoods"; "Review and amend the Delegation Bylaw"; expand residents' right to be informed and to appeal. Campaign table "Only Councillor to vote against" the Delegation Bylaw is her claim; no independent press URL opened this pass. FLAG, not a roll-call. No sourced miss, so no cap. [https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
54 M82/M82b community surveys, turnout and ballot access — The campaign voter survey is a campaign tool, not a City community-survey, advance-vote or ballot-access instrument. Mention of asking residents, so a dash. — —
55 M81 Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic) **Partial+ 1.5** "Gardiner called it “a farce” and called on council to insist that a binding question be put on the municipal ballot in 2030." Named NO, with Caradonna, Hammond and Thompson, on putting the non-binding question on the 2026 ballot, 5–4. Commits to a binding amalgamation vote. Comparable to M81, not Same (2030, not this ballot). The NO on the 2026 voter question is a sourced miss vs putting amalgamation to voters now, so the incumbent cap holds this cell below Close. Not Opposed: she is not against amalgamation; she wants a stronger later instrument. Do not treat Kim/Loughton YES as the only hit. [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-to-go-ahead-with-non-binding-amalgamation-question-12476505](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-to-go-ahead-with-non-binding-amalgamation-question-12476505) vote 25 Jun 2026 / press 27 Jun 2026
## Working notes (internal, not for the cell) - **Sources read in full:** [marggardiner.ca](https://marggardiner.ca/) home (retrieved 2026-09-02) · [/priorities/](https://marggardiner.ca/priorities/) · [/voting-record/](https://marggardiner.ca/voting-record/) · [ACTW profile](https://acitythatworks.ca/profiles/gardiner) · [City biography](https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/mayor-and-council/councillor-marg-gardiner) · Times Colonist Missing Middle 27 Jan 2023, daytime sheltering 19 Jul 2024, pay hike 2 Aug 2024, budget 9 May 2026, amalgamation 27 Jun 2026 · Victoria News budget 11 May 2026 · CHEK draft-budget 13 Mar 2026, VicPD 4→2 3 Mar 2026, Harbour 2 Jul 2026, salaries 13 Nov 2025 · [Saanich News canopy motion 4 Apr 2025](https://saanichnews.com/2025/04/04/a-developers-wet-dream-and-a-renters-nightmare-victoria-plans-for-growth/) · [City member motion, Urban Forest Canopy](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/filestream.ashx?DocumentId=101687) · [City 2026 budget page](https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/city-budget) (7.28 / 9.34 / 4.78). - **Not independently reconciled, not stamped:** campaign "reserves fell from over \$300 million to about \$160 million"; campaign 9.24% residential and 13.43% / \~17% 2027 figures. Lock remains 13.3 → 7.28 overall / 9.34 residential / 4.78 business. - **Not a source, applied:** BSc / MBA, 16 years on JBNA, chemistry and regulatory-enforcement background, "I don't take money from developers," third-party endorsements (Young, Gudgeon, Kidd, Scott, Gaultier), hanging-basket photo, granddaughter-at-City-Hall photo, Climate Action Task Force / airport / SIPP seats. - **One sentence, one measure — the ledger.** Thirteen sentences carry the thirteen scored cells: (1) amend MM to provincial minimum → row 1. (2) enforce existing bylaws → row 10. (3) enforce open drug-use laws in neighbourhoods → row 11. (4) do not shift encampments to neighbourhood parks → row 12. (5) COLA tax cap (priorities ZBB sentence; ZBB already on row 41) → row 13. (6) opposed to SCS and low-barrier supportive housing → row 23. (7) foot patrols and hiring of police officers → row 33. (8) "I will zero-base the budget" (homepage) → row 41. (9) green space / amenities by density → row 38. (10) increase canopy via plantings → row 49. (11) COLA-limit councillor/mayor pay → row 52. (12) re-introduce IAP2 → row 53. (13) binding amalgamation question in 2030 → row 55. - **Kim quote not copied.** 7 May 2026 NO is named for Gardiner, Kim and Hammond. Kim's reason ("the tax hike was simply not enough") is Kim's. Gardiner's named reasons are process ("fundamentally flawed," "no serious thought") and spending ("digging ourselves into a hole"; CHEK 13 Mar 2026: shifting costs to 2027 is "an election ploy").
